answer:
**Self-supervised vision creates a learning problem from images without needing a class label for each one.** SimCLR treats two augmentations of the same image as a positive pair and other images as negatives. MoCo maintains a momentum encoder and a queue to provide a large, more stable set of comparison features. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07193) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.06377)

BYOL and DINO use a student that matches a teacher's representation, with architectural and optimization mechanisms that discourage every image receiving the same output. The teacher is typically updated more slowly than the student. MAE instead hides many image patches and learns to reconstruct them from the visible patches, emphasizing prediction of missing content.

**Why object-like regions can emerge.** Different crops of an image may share an object while backgrounds vary. Learning consistent features across those views can favor representations organized around recurring visual entities. Patch-level interactions can then produce maps that highlight an object even without a segmentation label for every pixel.

An attractive attention map is not automatically a precise segmentation mask or a causal explanation. Evaluate the representation through downstream tasks such as linear classification, dense prediction, and transfer to new domains. Reconstruction, instance discrimination, and self-distillation encourage different information to be preserved. Whether a loss uses explicit negatives is only one design choice, not a complete explanation of representation quality.

**Technical details and references.**

SimCLR contrasts augmented views against negatives; MoCo maintains a momentum encoder/queue for negatives. BYOL and DINO use teacher–student consistency with mechanisms that discourage collapse, without explicit negative pairs. MAE reconstructs masked image patches from visible ones. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07193) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.06377)

DINO-style features can organize object-related regions because augmentations, patch interactions, and self-distillation encourage shared semantic structure. Attention maps can highlight objects, but they are not guaranteed segmentation masks or causal explanations. DINOv2 also depends on data curation and its specific training objectives.

Compare linear probing, dense prediction, robustness, and transfer with appropriate heads. A representation good for classification may not preserve all detail required for reconstruction. Evaluate the trained features rather than inferring capability from whether the loss uses negatives.
